steps.title: Tell us your story
steps.subtitle: A few lines is enough. We'll turn it into pages.

steps.title: Who is the book for?
steps.subtitle: This sets how many words go on each page.

options.name: Babies and toddlers
options.desc: Ages 0 to 3. Very few words, big simple pictures.
options.tip: Amazon prints paper pages, not thick board pages, so the book is best read with a grown-up.

options.name: Little kids
options.desc: Ages 3 to 7. Read aloud together at bedtime.
options.tip: This is the classic picture book age.

options.name: Early readers
options.desc: Ages 6 to 9. Short sentences kids read by themselves.

options.name: Big kids
options.desc: Ages 8 to 12. Short chapters with some pictures.

options.name: Teens
options.desc: Ages 13 and up. Longer stories with chapters.

options.name: Grown-ups
options.desc: Adult readers.

steps.title: What kind of book?
steps.subtitle: We picked the usual kind for this age.

options.name: Picture book
options.desc: A big picture on every page and a few lines of words.

options.name: Early reader
options.desc: Short, easy sentences and a picture on most pages.

options.name: Chapter book
options.desc: Short chapters with a few pictures.

options.name: Novel
options.desc: Mostly words, maybe a picture for each chapter.

steps.title: How should your book be made?
steps.subtitle: Pick one. The Kindle eBook is made for free with any choice.

options.name: Paperback
options.desc: Soft, bendy cover. Light and the cheapest to buy.
options.tip: Most picture books on Amazon are paperbacks. We'll make the Kindle version too. Hardcover is offered for longer books (75+ pages).

options.name: Hardcover
options.desc: Thick, stiff cover that lasts for years. Great as a gift.
options.tip: Hardcovers last for years and feel special. Amazon makes them for books of 75 to 550 pages, in black and white or bright color.

options.name: eBook only
options.desc: Read on a Kindle, tablet, or phone. Nothing to ship.
options.tip: Pictures look bright on a screen. You can still add a printed book later.

steps.title: How big should the book be?
steps.subtitle: Shown to scale next to a child's hand.

options.name: Square
options.desc: 8.5 × 8.5 inches. The classic picture book shape.

options.name: Tall
options.desc: 8 × 10 inches. Room for big pictures and words.

options.name: Large
options.desc: 8.5 × 11 inches. Like a sheet of printer paper.

options.name: Pocket
options.desc: 5 × 8 inches. Small and easy to carry.

options.name: Classic
options.desc: 5.5 × 8.5 inches. A common chapter book size.

options.name: Standard
options.desc: 6 × 9 inches. The most common book size.

steps.title: How many pages?
steps.subtitle: Includes the title page and the end page.

options.name: 24 pages
options.desc: Short and sweet. Amazon's smallest book.

options.name: 32 pages
options.desc: The classic picture book length.

options.name: 40 pages
options.desc: A little more room for the story.

options.name: 48 pages
options.desc: A longer story with more pictures.

options.name: 64 pages
options.desc: A long early reader.

options.name: Let the story decide
options.desc: We'll count the pages once the chapters are written.

steps.title: How should the inside be printed?
steps.subtitle: The same page printed three ways.

options.name: Bright color
options.desc: The richest colors. Best for picture books.

options.name: Everyday color
options.desc: Cheaper, with colors a little less bright.

warn.text: Amazon needs at least 72 pages for everyday color. Pick Bright color for a shorter book.

options.name: Black and white
options.desc: The cheapest. For books with few or no color pictures.

warn.text: The pictures will print in shades of gray.

options.name: White
options.desc: Bright white pages. Colors look their best.

options.name: Cream
options.desc: Soft, warm pages that are easy on the eyes for long reading.

steps.title: Shiny or soft cover?
steps.subtitle: How the outside of the cover feels.

options.name: Glossy
options.desc: Shiny and bright. Wipes clean, great for little hands.

options.name: Matte
options.desc: Soft and smooth, with no shine. Feels elegant.

steps.title: What should the pictures look like?
steps.subtitle: The same little scene drawn in each style.

options.name: Watercolor
options.desc: Soft, gentle paint. Classic bedtime story feel.
options.tip_no_service: Claude paints this itself with soft washes and paper texture. An image service makes richer, more detailed paintings.

options.name: Cartoon
options.desc: Bold lines and bright colors, like a TV show.
options.tip_no_service: Claude draws bold outlines and bright colors itself. This style works well without an image service.

options.name: Crayon
options.desc: Looks hand-drawn by a child with crayons.
options.tip_no_service: Claude draws waxy crayon texture itself. It looks hand-made, which suits this style.

options.name: 3D
options.desc: Round, shiny characters, like an animated movie.
options.tip_no_service: Claude draws round, shaded shapes. They're simpler than a real 3D look; an image service makes that.

options.name: Line art
options.desc: Black outlines only. Kids can color it in.
options.tip_no_service: Claude draws clean outlines itself. This style works very well without an image service.

options.name: Colored pencil
options.desc: Soft pencil strokes. Matches kids' own drawings.
options.tip_no_service: Claude shades with pencil-like strokes itself. Great next to children's own drawings.

options.name: Simple shapes
options.desc: Clean, flat shapes drawn by Claude. Free, no image service.
options.tip_no_service: Claude's best style. Clean, consistent and sharp, with no image service needed.

steps.title: Do you have your own drawings?
steps.subtitle: You can add them after the words are written.

options.name: Make all the pictures
options.desc: We'll draw every picture in the style you picked.

options.name: I have drawings
options.desc: Add your own drawings for any pages, the cover, or the characters.
options.tip: After the words are ready, a page opens where you add photos of the drawings and choose how much to improve each one.

steps.title: Where do the words go?
steps.subtitle: How pictures and words share the page.

options.name: Words in a box
options.desc: The picture fills the page. Words sit in a soft box.

options.name: Words below
options.desc: Picture on top, words underneath.

options.name: Words beside
options.desc: Words on one page, the picture on the facing page.

options.name: Picture per chapter
options.desc: Pages of words, with a picture at the start of each chapter.

steps.title: How should the story feel?
steps.subtitle: Not sure? We can tell from your story.

options.name: Let the story decide
options.desc: We'll read your story and match its feeling.

options.name: Funny
options.desc: Silly moments and giggles.

options.name: Cozy
options.desc: Warm, gentle, and kind.

options.name: Adventurous
options.desc: Exciting, brave, and full of surprises.

options.name: Sleepy
options.desc: Calm and quiet, perfect for bedtime.

steps.title: Anything extra?
steps.subtitle: Tap to add or remove. You can pick more than one.

options.name: Dedication
options.desc: A short note at the front, like "For Grandma".

options.name: The End page
options.desc: A last page that says The End.

options.name: About the author
options.desc: A few lines about who wrote the book.

options.name: Questions to talk about
options.desc: Fun questions for after reading together.

steps.title: How much do you want to check?
steps.subtitle: You can always change things at the end.

options.name: Check as we go
options.desc: Approve the title and words, then the pictures, then the final book.

options.name: Surprise me
options.desc: Make the whole book, then show me at the end.

steps.title: Here's your book
steps.subtitle: Tap Change on anything you'd like to fix.
